questions.title: Who will win the women's singles title at the 2026 Canadian Open?
questions.background: The Canadian Open is a major hard-court tennis tournament held during the build-up to the US Open.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The official WTA results for the 2026 Canadian Open will determine the women's singles champion. Resolution Timing : The question resolves when the tournament's women's singles final is completed and its result is officially recorded. Accepted Answer Format : Provide the winning player's full name.

French Open champion Mirra Andreeva (World No. 5, 37-11 in 2026, rested since Wimbledon R2) trims slightly 0.09 -> 0.08. Top-5 sum = 0.57, preserving 0.43 outside for Swiatek (~0.07), newly crowned Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova (~0.06, World No. 7), 2024 Toronto finalist Amanda Anisimova (~0.045), 2025 finalist Naomi Osaka (~0.045, beat Sabalenka at Wimbledon), Marta Kostyuk (~0.04, 21-2 in last 23 matches), Elina Svitolina (~0.03), and wide 96-player WTA 1000 field variance.

questions.title: Which two countries will reach the final of the 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations?
questions.background: The Women's Africa Cup of Nations is Africa's continental championship for women's national football teams. The winners of its two semifinals advance to the final.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : CAF's official tournament results, supported where necessary by contemporaneous match reporting. Resolution : Resolve once both semifinals of the 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations have concluded and the two finalists have been determined. The result of the final itself is not relevant. Accepted Answer Format : The two finalist country names in alphabetical order, separated by a comma.
questions.current_reasoning: The expanded 16-team 2026 WAFCON runs July 26–August 16 in Morocco (Rabat and Casablanca), with the knockout bracket placing A1/B2/D1/C2 in SF1 and B1/A2/C1/D2 in SF2. As Group A favorites and hosts, Morocco are projected on the opposite side of the bracket from defending 10-time champions Nigeria (Group C) and 2022 champions South Africa (Group B), who are projected to collide in SF2—suppressing a Nigeria–South Africa final unless one finishes second in its group. Crucially, Nigeria and Zambia share Group C, meaning whichever finishes first and second go to opposite halves and can meet in the final; a bracket-consistent Monte Carlo simulation places 60% mass across these top five finalist pairings and 40% across Cameroon and other combinations.

questions.title: Which country will win the 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations?
questions.background: The Women’s Africa Cup of Nations is Africa’s continental championship for senior women’s national football teams.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The Confederation of African Football’s official result for the 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations final. Resolution : Resolve to the country whose national team is declared champion following the final. Accepted Answer Format : The country’s name.
questions.current_reasoning: Defending champions Nigeria (10-time winners who beat Morocco 3–2 in the 2024/25 final) remain Africa's deepest and highest-ranked side, making them 40% favorites despite a tricky Group C with Zambia and a projected semifinal against South Africa. Three-time consecutive hosts Morocco (23%) enjoy Rabat home advantage, back-to-back final pedigree, and a favorable Group A and SF1 bracket half. 2022 champions South Africa (16%), explosive attackers Zambia led by Barbra Banda and Racheal Kundananji (9%), and Pot 1 side Ghana (5%) round out the top five (93% total), with 7% left for Cameroon and dark horses.

questions.title: Which DRC province will WHO identify as experiencing a surge in weekly Ebola cases in mid-September 2026?
questions.background: The Democratic Republic of Congo declared an Ebola outbreak in May 2026.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : WHO public statements about the DRC Ebola outbreak, including statements quoted in contemporaneous reputable news reporting. Resolution Window : Resolve to the province explicitly identified by WHO as experiencing surging weekly Ebola cases in its outbreak assessment publicly reported between September 10 and September 16, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the province.
questions.current_reasoning: Hard provincial data from DRC INSP SitRep 073 (published July 27, data to July 26: 3,262 cases, 1,437 deaths) alongside July 30 Al Jazeera/AP updates (3,442 confirmed cases, 1,521 deaths—a 50% one-week death spike with 50 deaths in 24 hours; Uganda declared Ebola-free July 28): (1) North Kivu overtakes Ituri for #1 (0.29 -> 0.35) after reaching 314 confirmed cases and 204 deaths, with Ebola treatment center bed occupancy jumping from 120% (July 21) to 136.2% (192 patients for 141 beds) plus 11 infected health workers—signaling an accelerating secondary wave in Katwa/Butembo/M23-affected corridors well positioned for a mid-September WHO weekly surge call. (2) Ituri remains strong at #2 (0.32 -> 0.31) with 2,901 cases (88.9% of total) and 1,207 deaths amid July 28 Bunia health worker strikes, the Nyakunde facility attack, and 60.9% community deaths. (3) Haut-Uele rises to #3 (0.13 -> 0.15) with 38 confirmed cases and formal inclusion in the expanded four-province UN Ebola response appeal. (4) Tshopo drops sharply to #4 (0.19 -> 0.12) after holding flat at 5 confirmed cases with zero new cases from July 21 to July 26, confirming containment of Kisangani's imported cluster so far while retaining river-corridor re-introduction risk. (5) South Kivu stays at 0.02 (3 cumulative cases, 61 consecutive days with zero new cases; 5% residual for Bas-Uele/Maniema/Kinshasa).

local_articles.title: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo ‘intensifying’: WHO
local_articles.snippet: in a statement. The deadliest Ebola outbreak in the DRC killed nearly 2,300 out of almost 3,500 recorded cases between 2018 and 2020. The current outbreak was declared on May 15 and is caused by the Bundibugyo strain of the virus, for which there is no approved vaccine or treatment. As at July 30, a total of 3,605 confirmed cases, including 1,587 deaths, had been reported in the DRC, according to the WHO, indicating a case fatality rate of 44 per cent. The outbreak is “intensifying, with sustained transmission and continued increases in reported cases and deaths”, the WHO warned. Ebola, which spreads through contact with bodily fluids and causes haemorrhagic fever, has killed more than 15,000 people across Africa over the past 50 years. questions.title: Who will win the lightweight co-main event at UFC 331?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : UFC's official results or contemporaneous reporting of the lightweight co-main event at UFC 331, scheduled for September 19, 2026. Resolution : Resolve to the fighter officially declared the winner of that bout on fight night. Subsequent changes to the result will not affect resolution. Accepted Answer Format : The winning fighter's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: The UFC 331 lightweight co-main event (Sept 19) has not yet been announced, and pairing it under a flyweight title bout strongly indicates a non-title contender fight rather than new champion Justin Gaethje vs. Ilia Topuria (who fought a brutal war on June 14 leaving Topuria with two broken orbital bones). With Max Holloway, Paddy Pimblett, and Benoit Saint Denis all booked for UFC 329 on July 11, healthy top contenders Arman Tsarukyan (#1 contender, idle since Nov 2025), star former champ Charles Oliveira, surging Mauricio Ruffy (up to #9 after beating Michael Chandler June 14), Dan Hooker, and Mateusz Gamrot are prime co-main candidates. Because booking uncertainty across ~10-12 ranked lightweights is high, top-5 probabilities sum conservatively to 56%.

questions.title: Which major US employment sector will shed the most jobs in July 2026?
questions.background: The US Bureau of Labor Statistics reports monthly changes in nonfarm payroll employment by sector.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the broad employment sector with the largest net decline in payroll jobs in July 2026, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics' initial employment report for that month, released in August 2026. Resolution Date : 2026-08-07 Accepted Answer Format : Compare sectors by the number of jobs lost, not percentage changes, and count subsectors within their parent sectors. Answer with the sector's name.
questions.current_reasoning: First major update since July 2 incorporating mid-to-late July 2026 US labor and macro data: (1) S&P Global US Flash PMI (July 24, CFO Dive/Trading Economics) jumped to an 8-month high of 53.6 from 51.9, driven by services resuming hiring for the first time in 3 months, while manufacturing slowed to its weakest production growth since March as the resumed US-Iran war (July 7) pushed supplier delays to a ~4-year high and input inflation to a 14-month high; (2) weekly initial jobless claims for the July 12-18 BLS survey week plunged 22k to 187,000 (July 23 Reuters/Straits Times), signaling healthy aggregate private demand; (3) Deloitte Insights (July 19) and FactCheck.org (July 28) confirm federal payrolls fell 324,000 since Jan 2025 (-36k in H1 2026), manufacturing continued declining despite tariffs, gasoline topped $4/gal post-July 7, real spending on food services/accommodation fell two straight quarters ahead of June's -54.6k plunge, while Professional and business services (+23k/mo avg in H1 2026) and wholesale/retail trade actually expanded. With broad private services rebounding, shrinking/shocked and seasonally volatile sectors rise to the top: holding Leisure and hospitality #1 at 0.18 (slightly down from 0.20 on mean-reversion/services PMI rebound, offset by weak dining demand, World Cup winding down from 16 to 4 venues in the survey week, and $4+ gas); lifting Government 0.13 -> 0.17 (persistent federal cuts + huge July state/local education seasonal swings); bringing Manufacturing into the top 5 at 0.15 (replacing Professional and business services, which drops to ~0.09 in residual given H1 +23k/mo trend) on Iran-war supply shocks, ongoing tariff-era contraction, and July auto retooling variance; trimming Financial activities 0.16 -> 0.15 (ongoing YoY contraction and fintech cuts like PayPal/Block/today's Visa 2,600 layoff announcement, though Visa cuts hit later months) and Trade, transportation, and utilities 0.16 -> 0.14 (29M base + $4+ gas tempered by positive 2026 trade trend). 21% residual covers PBS (~9%), Information (~5%), Construction (~4%), Other services (~2%), and others (~1%).
